alerts.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 18 at 1:36AM EDT until October 22 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL

text.name: Sunday Night
text.detail: Showers and thunderstorms likely before 9pm, then a chance of showers and thunderstorms between 9pm and 11pm, then a chance of showers and thunderstorms between 11pm and 1am, then a slight chance of showers and thunderstorms between 1am and 5am. Mostly cloudy, with a low around 74. Northeast wind 16 to 22 mph, with gusts as high as 32 mph. Chance of precipitation is 60%. New rainfall amounts between a half and three quarters of an inch possible.

text.name: Monday
text.detail: Mostly sunny, with a high near 85. Northeast wind around 21 mph, with gusts as high as 30 mph.

text.name: Monday Night
text.detail: A slight chance of rain showers before 2am. Partly cloudy, with a low around 73. Northeast wind 13 to 20 mph, with gusts as high as 28 mph. Chance of precipitation is 20%.

source.table: National Weather Service heat index categories
source.verified: Chart read by hand: the chart is an image and could not be machine-read. Confirm the boundaries and wording against the NWS chart before relying on them.

bands.name: Below caution
bands.action: Below the heat index of 80 F where OSHA's extra heat precautions start. Drink water as usual.

bands.name: Caution
bands.effects: Fatigue is possible with long exposure or activity.
bands.action: Extra heat precautions apply from 80 F (OSHA). Drink water about every 15 minutes. Take rest breaks in the shade.

bands.name: Extreme caution
bands.rest: Frequent rest breaks in the shade.
bands.effects: Heat cramps, heat exhaustion or heat stroke are possible with long exposure or activity.
bands.action: Drink water about every 15 minutes. Take frequent rest breaks in the shade. Watch the crew for heat illness signs.

bands.name: Danger
bands.rest: Frequent rest breaks in the shade.
bands.effects: Heat cramps and heat exhaustion are likely. Heat stroke is probable with continued activity.
bands.action: Drink water about every 15 minutes. Take frequent rest breaks in the shade. Do the heaviest work in the cooler hours.

bands.name: Extreme danger
bands.rest: Frequent rest breaks in the shade.
bands.action: Move work out of these hours where you can. Where you cannot, drink water about every 15 minutes and take frequent rest breaks in the shade.

water_plan.name: Caution
water_plan.action: Extra heat precautions apply from 80 F (OSHA). Drink water about every 15 minutes. Take rest breaks in the shade.

source.verified: Taken from NIOSH and OSHA pages as summarised by a search tool on 2026-10-18. Confirm against the pages before relying on it.

acclimatization.who: OSHA treats workers as unacclimatized when they have been on the job less than 1 to 2 weeks. NIOSH treats workers back after an absence of more than a week as new.

new.label: New workers
new.unit: percent of the usual time in the heat

experienced.label: Experienced workers, first days back
experienced.unit: percent of the usual time in the heat

notes: New workers start at no more than 20% of the usual time in the heat on day 1 and add no more than 20% each day.
Supervise new workers closely for the first 14 days or until they are fully acclimatized.
In a sudden heat wave, even experienced workers start the first hot day at 50% of the usual time.
For intense work, take frequent rest breaks and do the work in the cooler part of the day (OSHA).
The heat index assumes shade. In full sun it can be up to 15 F higher (NWS), so the sun column shows the upper case.
Hourly values are the highest of seven forecast points within 20 km of the site.
WBGT is an approximation and its tiers are not verified against TB MED 507.
OSHA treats workers as unacclimatized when they have been on the job less than 1 to 2 weeks. Use the acclimatization switch.

caveats: The score is the chance that NOAA records a severe event of that kind near the plant, weighted by how often OSHA injuries follow. It is not a count of injuries.
The model was trained on 60 power plants and on reanalysis weather, then scored on live forecasts.
In tests the fire model did not beat a simple seasonal average. Do not act on a fire driver alone.

mud.label: STRAM-inspired, uncalibrated. Prioritizes inspection; does not certify a crossing is safe.
caveats: STRAM-inspired, uncalibrated. Prioritizes inspection; does not certify a crossing is safe.
1 pass is below the study's observed range (2-80 passes): mild extrapolation of Eq 5 (Z = a/NCI_adj).
Only unpaved ways in OpenStreetMap are rated. Paved roads and private haul roads are not.

bands.name: Moderate
bands.meaning: Air quality is acceptable. Some people who are unusually sensitive may be affected.

bands.name: Unhealthy for sensitive groups
bands.meaning: People with lung or heart disease, older adults and children are the most at risk.

bands.name: Unhealthy
bands.meaning: Everyone may begin to have health effects. Sensitive groups may have more serious effects.

bands.name: Very unhealthy
bands.meaning: Everyone may have health effects. Sensitive groups may have serious effects.

bands.name: Hazardous
bands.meaning: Everyone may have serious health effects.

notes: Air quality is a model forecast, not a sensor reading.

source.name: Open-Meteo air quality (CAMS) and the AirNow AQI scale

caveats: Roads come from OpenStreetMap. Private haul roads, gates, closures, weight limits and truck heights are often missing.
Only unpaved ways are rated by the mud model. A detour can use paved roads that are not rated.
A detour is a suggestion from map data. Check it on the ground.
Sightings are reported by volunteers and are denser near towns and trails. A month with few sightings can mean few observers.
No sightings does not mean no animals. Plan for wildlife on every wet or vegetated site.
The species list is a starter list and needs confirming for the region.

systems.name: L-31 East
systems.flood_sources: Inundation by normal ocean tides. Everglades National Park

caveats: The National Levee Database maps levees. It does not say whether a levee will hold on the report day.
Local or non-USACE levees can be missing from the database.
'Not rated' means USACE has no inspection rating for the system. It does not mean the levee is sound.
Tide and flood shading in this report ignores levees on purpose. Treat a leveed area as able to flood.

tide.time_zone: Local time at the station (standard or daylight)
tide.datum: MLLW (mean lower low water), metres and feet above it
caveats: Estimate from predicted tide and a 10 m ground model. It ignores storm surge, river level, rain, drains, levees and ground-model error. Ground not shaded is not guaranteed dry.
The tide station was chosen by distance and has not been confirmed by a person.
